name: Bonapartism
summary: Bonapartism is rule by a charismatic leader who claims to embody the people's will, combining a strong centralised state, army and bureaucracy with plebiscitary legitimacy. It promises to end revolutionary disorder and class conflict, reconcile authority with popular rights and 1789 equality, and deliver national glory and material progress through state-led growth, while suppressing organised opposition.
scope: The Napoleonic idea as put by Louis-Napoleon (Napoleon III) and practised in the Second Empire (1852-1870), with the Napoleon I tradition behind it; Marx's Eighteenth Brumaire is used as a critical analysis of its class base. Excludes the broad modern use of the word for any military strongman and later neo-Bonapartist or Gaullist strands. No Bonapartist primary text was opened, so self-description rests on reference summaries of Des idees napoleoniennes and the 1852 constitution.

sources.title: Bonapartism

sources.usedFor: Definition: authoritarian centralised state under a charismatic strongman, traditionalist ideology; narrow and Marxian senses.

sources.author: Karl Marx (1852)
sources.usedFor: Contemporary critical analysis of the class base: small-holding peasants, bureaucracy, army, clergy, property and order. Written by an opponent, so used for structure rather than self-description.

sources.usedFor: Constitutional design: powerful president, command of forces, ministers, weak Legislative Body, unlimited terms, plebiscites.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Second Empire's paternalist social policy (worker housing, mutual aid) that a state guarantee would be accepted but not as a right.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No wage floors existed; the regime favored arbitration boards and cheap bread rather than statutory wages, so adherents plausibly split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Empire used state investment in railways, ports and credit institutions to steer growth, though it also opened trade; markets were a tool, not the arbiter.

public-ownership.rationale: Railways were built through state-backed concessions to private companies rather than nationalized; no doctrine of public ownership, and no principled bar either.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The regime sought support from both propertied and poor; no documented stance on steeply progressive taxation.

unions-good.rationale: Coalition (strike) rights were granted only in 1864 under state oversight, and independent labor organization stayed policed; unions were tolerated, not championed.

property-fundamental.rationale: Marx portrays Bonapartism as the champion of order and property, resting on the small-holding peasant; the state still defended it as the basis of social order.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Empire promoted joint-stock banks and investment while the state kept guiding the economy; no clear doctrine either way.

cut-welfare.rationale: Louis-Napoleon wrote on extinguishing pauperism by state action and the Empire funded worker housing and relief, so cutting welfare runs against its paternalism.

worker-ownership.rationale: Napoleon III's social policy aimed at improving workers' lot through state-led paternalism and arbitration, not collective ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Second Empire was a police state with press censorship and mass arrests of opponents, justified by security and order.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the authoritarian, order-minded character of the regime that permissive drug policy would be rejected.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not a concept of the era; the regime restricted speech heavily for political order, but the statement's aim (protecting groups) is not its rationale.

strong-leader.rationale: Definitional: Bonapartism is the rule of a charismatic strongman who bypasses parliamentary deadlock, as at the 1851 coup.

state-harmful.rationale: Bonapartism favors an authoritarian centralised state; the idea that the state is unnecessary is the opposite.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; the regime disarmed and disbanded the republican National Guard and policed dissent, suggesting acceptance of state control of arms.

empower-police-military.rationale: The regime rested on army and police, reorganized the National Guard, and relied on the armed forces as a pillar of the state.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Second Empire France regulated prostitution through police; no ideological position, adherents plausibly split.

decide-locally.rationale: Bonapartism centralizes authority in the leader and the state; prefects appointed from Paris embodied this.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; the regime transported thousands of opponents to Cayenne and Algeria, indicating a punitive posture.

traditional-family.rationale: Bonapartism is described as relatively traditionalist; the Napoleonic Civil Code upheld patriarchal family authority.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the traditionalist, order-oriented ideology and a Napoleonic legal tradition of patriarchal family law.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from traditionalist leanings and the Napoleonic penal code that criminalized abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: Bonapartism treated religion as a support for order: priests as an instrument of government (Marx), and Napoleon III courted Catholics.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; Bonapartism stresses formal equality before the law, not remedial programs, so adherents would likely decline.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from traditionalist family views of the Napoleonic tradition.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Appeals to national glory and the Napoleonic legend are core to Bonapartist identity and its traditionalist strain.

gradual-change.rationale: Bonapartism came to power by coup and plebiscite yet claims to end revolution and stabilize order; adherents are split between rupture and continuity.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Second Empire's pro-growth, open-trade stance that restriction was not a priority.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Napoleon III proposed a European congress for arbitration, but his vision was nation-states under French leadership, not empowered bodies.

free-trade.rationale: The 1860 Cobden-Chevalier treaties lowered tariffs but were bilateral and kept protections; the position was pragmatic, not doctrinal.

nation-first.rationale: French interest and prestige drove Second Empire foreign policy, e.g., gaining Nice and Savoy for aiding Italy, though cooperation was used when useful.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Interventions in Syria and elsewhere were framed partly humanitarian, but motives were mixed and adherents would split.

open-borders.rationale: A centralised, nation-state ideology resting on national glory has no place for open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The Empire prized growth through railways, credit and public works as legitimating achievements.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; a state-directed ideology could accept state action but nothing in it supplies a stance.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The Napoleonic idea was described as social and industrial; the regime promoted railways, credit and technological modernization.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from state-led industrial modernization and a strong-state approach to energy.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bonapartism claims to close the revolution and restore order; Marx depicts it as counter-revolutionary, though it came to power by coup.

experts-over-public.rationale: The regime governed through an appointed Council of State and administrators, yet claimed popular sovereignty through plebiscites; adherents split.

central-planning.rationale: The state directed investment but kept private enterprise and open trade, so full central planning is rejected.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the movement shows no doctrine on how firms are owned.

land-value-tax.rationale: No documented stance; the Empire's finances were conventional and nothing in its ideology addresses a single land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from its role as defender of small property and family patrimony among peasants.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; the regime's paternalism favored work, relief and housing, not unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Empire shifted to free-trade treaties in 1860 while retaining some protections; Napoleon I's tradition was protectionist, so strands differ.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state invested heavily in railways, ports, canals and credit institutions as a defining feature of Second Empire economic policy.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Marx identifies the small-holding peasant as Bonapartism's class base, and its property policy aimed to spread ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Bonapartism upholds the existing social order and property; abolishing money and wages is the opposite of its aims.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A statist regime that built credit institutions such as the Crédit Foncier and Crédit Mobilier would reject abolition.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Arbitration boards and a state role in labor relations existed, yet no doctrine of state-recognized bodies setting wages and prices.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bonapartism rules through one man and plebiscites, not a party guided by ideology; official candidates existed but no ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Bonapartism sought an hereditary imperial dynasty, but legitimated by plebiscite rather than divine right.

democracy-best.rationale: Bonapartism claims popular sovereignty but with no free parliament; it held that democracy needed to be incarnated in one man.

direct-votes.rationale: The regime repeatedly used plebiscites to ratify the coup, constitution and empire, so direct votes on regime questions are central, though not on ordinary laws.

workers-councils.rationale: Marx depicts Bonapartism as built on peasants, army and bureaucracy against workers' movements; councils would be anathema.

right-to-secede.rationale: A centralised unitary state led by a national leader rejects secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Bonapartism's stress on a providential leader reflects belief that some are marked to lead.

political-violence-never.rationale: The regime itself came to power by coup, with about 26,000 arrests, and defended order by force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Napoleonic glory was central, but Napoleon III argued military successes are temporary and public opinion wins the final victory.

separate-church-state.rationale: The regime treated the clergy as an instrument of government and a pillar of order, not a separate sphere.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Napoleonic tradition is a secular, civil-code order; religion supports order but laws do not derive from scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Authoritarian centralised state monopoly of force and justice; privatization is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Army-backed regime seeking French grandeur and glory; military power was central to both Napoleons.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Napoleon III's nationality principle was about peoples' self-government, but France's civic Napoleonic tradition is not ethnic.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Bonapartism claims to stand above classes, conciliating them; class conflict as history's engine is Marx's thesis against it.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The regime promised protection of the diligent and needy and equality before the law, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; the Empire expanded colonial rule in Algeria and elsewhere.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The Second Empire doubled the colonial empire, so reparations are not in its outlook.

civilizational-union.rationale: Napoleon III favored nation-states under French leadership, not civilization blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Bonapartism stresses duty, glory and social order over self-interest as a moral ideal.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from its authority-and-order emphasis; the regime guaranteed 1789 principles on paper while limiting freedoms.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not addressed, and an era-specific silence.

limit-population.rationale: Anachronistic; a pro-natalist, grandeur-oriented state would likely not restrict births.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The regime staked its legitimacy on industrial, railway and urban modernization.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Modernization was favored but within established institutions and order, so disruption is not welcomed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic with no basis for a position.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from personal rule by a charismatic leader as core.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the police-state approach to security and censorship.

restore-past-order.rationale: Bonapartism claims to reconcile order with progress; it restores order but not a lost past one, so adherents split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Napoleonic idea was described as reconciling order and freedom pragmatically; Bonapartism often claims to transcend left and right.

direct-action.rationale: Bonapartism condemns disorder and relies on the state, though Louis-Napoleon seized power by coup rather than elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Bonapartism is willing to use coup and repression to reach stability, so means need not mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Opposed to its modernizing, industrial program.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A state promoting industry and credit has no reason to abolish it.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The Empire offered paternalist relief but rewarded the diligent; need-based distribution as principle isn't Bonapartist.

production-for-use.rationale: The Empire promoted joint-stock, profit-oriented enterprise alongside state direction.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marx's thesis; Bonapartism poses as protector of bourgeois society and property.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marx's analysis shows Bonapartism as counter-revolutionary against working-class rule.

collective-farming.rationale: It rests on the small-holding peasantry, who own their plots.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist thesis opposed by a regime that pursued wars for national glory and market opening within capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: An authoritarian statist regime financing public works through taxes and loans.

harm-principle.rationale: The state restricted press, teaching and assembly broadly to maintain order, beyond harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The regime stressed the people as a collective sovereign and the nation, though it affirmed 1789 principles.

conscription.rationale: The Napoleonic tradition rests on the nation in arms and the Second Empire kept conscription via lottery with replacement.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The regime relied on mass voting, even if staged, and a strong state, not on exit.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is an engine of national greatness and social direction, not a firm with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Louis-Napoleon wrote on lifting the working classes materially, but did not frame it as freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: The regime censored the press and could dismiss professors, indicating it saw them as threats to power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a Bonapartist doctrine; the civic Napoleonic tradition cut against racial theory.

organic-representation.rationale: The Senate and Council of State were appointed bodies, yet voting was by individual direct universal male suffrage.

total-state.rationale: Authoritarian and centralised but not totalitarian; the regime kept private enterprise and a non-political society.

national-rebirth.rationale: Bonapartists promised national greatness after revolutionary turmoil, but it was framed as restoration of order and glory, not decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Second Empire gained Nice and Savoy, doubled colonies, and sought the Rhine; expansion was pursued opportunistically.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule rested on a personal oath to the emperor as well as popular ratification; but not feudal bonds.

bound-labor.rationale: The Napoleonic tradition abolished feudal bonds in law and rests on free peasant proprietors.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; the regime's control of universities suggests knowledge was an instrument, but it claimed no such doctrine.

universal-morality.rationale: Inferred from Napoleonic Enlightenment-derived legal codes claiming universal principles of 1789.

single-common-good.rationale: The Napoleonic idea aims to reconcile and unite classes under one national interest embodied by the leader, rather than group bargaining.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed by the movement, with no basis for a stance.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Never addressed by Bonapartism; no source gives a position, so it is left neutral.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; paternalism favored, not democratic control of firms.

school-vouchers.rationale: Inferred from the centralizing university system under state control, from which the Education Minister could dismiss professors.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Empire financed public works with loans and state-backed credit, accepting deficits for growth.

economic-freedom.rationale: The regime coupled economic activity with political repression, treating political liberty as secondary.

rule-by-example.rationale: The regime used censorship, police and plebiscites, not moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Napoleon III made the principle of nationalities central, backing Italian and Romanian unification and using plebiscites.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; the Second Empire acted unilaterally in Mexico and Italy as French interest dictated.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Napoleonic idea mixes Enlightenment rationalism with a courting of the church; adherents split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from its praise of the diligent and needy and a work-centered paternalism.

class-collaboration.rationale: Bonapartism presents itself as above classes reconciling them; Marx notes it poses as protector of all.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Bonapartism rests on national tradition and the Napoleonic legend; Haussmann's Paris aside, culture is revered.

dominated-front.rationale: Napoleon III sought French leadership within Western alliances, such as with Britain in Crimea.

workers-nation.rationale: Bonapartism ties workers to the nation and the leader rather than an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Napoleonic Code treated men and women unequally in public and family law.

ban-interest.rationale: The Empire promoted investment banks, credit institutions and the stock market.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts the equality before the law inherited from 1789 and the Napoleonic Code.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marx held that Bonapartism made the state seem autonomous from classes; adherents claim it serves the whole nation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from industrial growth orientation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from the Napoleonic civic, centralizing, uniform legal approach to citizenship.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory not part of the tradition.

proportional-representation.rationale: The 1852 regime used gerrymanders and official candidates and a weak assembly; strong executive favoured over party-proportional bodies.

national-mission.rationale: French civilizing and Revolutionary legacy mission is part of the Napoleonic legend, but Napoleon III stressed nationalities' self-government.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Adherents would not frame the Napoleonic family order as systemic male advantage.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Bonapartism rises against the parliamentary elites by appealing to the people over the politicians, though the regime was itself corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the doctrine and anachronistic.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The regime shielded its police and army after the coup and mass arrests.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Second Empire was an interventionist state in the economy and society.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts the Napoleonic tradition of civic equality; no racial doctrine.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 1852 constitution affirmed the principles of 1789, including equality before the law, within a hierarchical regime.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not a Bonapartist issue; hostile to socialism so the claim is rejected loosely.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The Second Empire colonized Algeria and expanded colonial rule.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The Napoleonic Code is the emblem of the tradition: one civil law for all citizens.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Napoleonic settlement guaranteed freedom of worship for recognized faiths under the Concordat.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The regime kept the clergy influential in schooling and as an instrument of order.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not a socialist state, but inferred from its premise that a strong state, army and bureaucracy are the guarantee of order against hostile powers.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Bonapartism rests legitimacy on plebiscites and popular sovereignty, even if staged.

trade-surplus.rationale: Not stated, though free-trade treaties pursued exports; mercantilist tradition under Napoleon I.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement came to power by a coup and fought wars of choice.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not an explicit doctrine; the regime favoured both enterprise and conciliation.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The regime suppressed republican and socialist opposition after 1851 and defended the order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The regime itself held arbitrary power over subjects through decree and police.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1852 constitution concentrated power in the executive and left a weak legislature that could neither amend laws nor censure ministers.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist idea rejected by Bonapartism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Louis-Napoleon wrote on abolishing pauperism and the Empire claimed love of the diligent and needy.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: No documented stance, though it promoted worker housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were banned until 1864 and then permitted; both stances occur.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Louis-Napoleon blamed poverty on social organization and proposed state remedies.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Never addressed; the civic, uniform-law Napoleonic tradition neither asserts nor denies this, so it is left neutral.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Appointed prefects, senators and councillors under a personal ruler.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The regime suspended protections and mass-arrested opponents after the coup.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The Empire lowered bread prices, using state action for the poor.

party-controls-media.rationale: Press censorship from 1852 shows government control, though by state not party.

party-commands-army.rationale: The leader commands the army as head of state, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Never addressed in the sources; no stated position on citizenship timelines, so left neutral.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not Bonapartist; deputies were notables and the regime stood against such populism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Napoleon III imagined nation-states under French leadership, not supranational union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 1852 constitution gave the president command of the armed forces and the right to appoint and dismiss ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Inferred from the Concordat tradition of an episcopal hierarchy with state control.

clerical-rule.rationale: The clergy serve as an instrument of government, not as rulers.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist position opposed to national and army loyalty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The regime censored press and theatre, though for political rather than moral reasons chiefly.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The 1852 constitution allowed unlimited 10-year terms, and it was central to the regime.

recall-officials.rationale: Executive officials answered to the leader, not recall votes.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Napoleon III built alliances with Britain, Piedmont and others.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The movement favored property for peasants but not banning rentals.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Empire relied on a professional army and a parade-only National Guard.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The peasantry was the electoral base, yet the regime urbanized Paris; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Napoleon III supported national unification principle for Italy and Romania.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Not documented; the regime distrusted professors and the press, but the sources do not give a view on educated people as such.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Not documented; the principle of nationalities implies equal peoples but French cultural pride remained.

death-penalty.rationale: The Second Empire kept capital punishment, and the regime was punitive toward opponents.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anachronistic with Napoleonic rationalism; no ideological basis.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The regime prosecuted works on moral grounds, such as Madame Bovary in 1857, but this is inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The Napoleonic Code introduced descent-based nationality, though France has also allowed soil-based rules; adherents split.

minority-language-support.rationale: The centralising Napoleonic tradition promotes uniform French.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Napoleonic tradition insists on uniform law over exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The regime prized order and conformity under authoritarian rule.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Empire sought to guarantee creditors through banks and finance, and Mexico was a debt intervention.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Louis-Napoleon dissolved the assembly and imposed a constitution by plebiscite, bypassing a constituent assembly.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Early Empire restricted political liberty while promoting economic growth as its legitimacy.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Anachronistic with no support in the movement.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the pursuit of military grandeur and independence.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Louis-Napoleon was elected president directly in 1848 and the regime ratified rule by plebiscite.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state steered credit institutions, so an independent central bank conflicts with the strong-executive tradition.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; the regime itself traded territory for gains in Italy, but no doctrine on ceding claimed homelands exists.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Order and property are defended, yet the state is paternalist; split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not addressed; a late Marxist debate with no bearing on the tradition.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; a state-led developmental regime could regulate but acts by executive decision, so no clear stance.

collective-defense.rationale: Inferred from the Second Empire's pursuit of independent French diplomacy, with alliances formed ad hoc rather than binding mutual-defence pacts.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from Napoleon III's principle of nationalities and use of plebiscites to legitimise territorial changes such as Nice and Savoy.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Inferred from the Napoleonic Concordat tradition that made clergy salaried and subject to the state.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The ruler claims to embody the people's will and is the political leader, not a neutral figurehead.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the centralised authoritarian state that defends national unity by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The movement stresses a strong centralised state, army and bureaucracy with uniform administration.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Napoleon III ruled by popular plebiscite, not divine descent, though the regime cultivated religious ceremony.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the regime pursued state-led growth without an income-tax debate.

character-from-environment.rationale: Inferred from its programme of education and public works to reconcile classes and end pauperism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The 1852 constitution made the Emperor responsible only to the French people and left him free of the legislature.

space-expansion.rationale: Inferred from its stress on national glory and material progress; the sources do not mention space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Inferred from the regime's concentration of power in the leader with plebiscites, not a blend of aristocracy and people.

leader-cult.rationale: Bonapartism rests on a charismatic leader embodying the nation, with a Napoleonic personality cult as a defining feature.

equal-parenting.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal Napoleonic Code tradition and the absence of any such presumption.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Bonapartism promises to end class conflict and reconcile classes under the leader; inferred from that.

land-redistribution.rationale: The regime relied on propertied peasants and 'religion, family, property'; redistribution would cut against that base.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Napoleon III backed the principle of nationalities but not claims based on nationals abroad as such; split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Napoleonic order was secular and state-controlled; legal punishment for leaving a religion is inferred as alien to it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a modernising state that expanded women's education.

common-currency.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; a unified-currency policy fits state-led economics but is not stated.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not addressed; Napoleon III favoured national self-determination in Europe rather than ancestry-based unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: A strongly centralised state and unitary nation make separate self-governing minority institutions unlikely; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: 1789-style equality before the law implies rights for minorities where they live; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Bonapartism rests on will, leadership and national glory rather than a materialist theory of history; inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: State-led growth favoured big enterprise yet the regime also wanted competition; not addressed.

no-bailouts.rationale: A state-led growth model implies public support for failing key firms; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rule rests on plebiscites and the leader embodying the people's will, so courts and bodies should not override it.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a hierarchical, authoritarian regime with traditional gender roles.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Napoleon III signed the 1860 Cobden-Chevalier free-trade treaty, so a closed bloc runs against the Second Empire's policy.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Napoleon III's social reforms gave workers the right to organise and strike, but trade-treaty standards were not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Ruled by order and material progress, not moral exhortation; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Bonapartism opposes revolutionary disorder; its own seizures of power were by coup, but it presents itself as ending revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: 1789 equality was kept but the Second Empire made the throne hereditary and restored titles; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Napoleonic cult of national glory and the Second Empire's centralised, state-directed schooling; no source addresses curriculum directly.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from Second Empire colonial expansion (Algeria, Cochinchina, Mexico adventure) justified as bringing progress; sources do not state a doctrine.

patriotic-education.rationale: The regime centred legitimacy on national glory and the Napoleonic legend, and the state controlled education to instil loyalty to the dynasty and nation.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the 1789 principle of equality before the law that Bonapartism claimed to preserve, which implies merit-based, race-blind treatment.

public-money-creation.rationale: Second Empire policy favoured state-sponsored credit institutions (Credit Mobilier, Credit Foncier) alongside private banking, so no clear stance on who creates money; adherents are not documented as split either way.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Bonapartism promised to end class conflict through state-led growth and credit, implying capitalism could be managed rather than collapse; inferred, not stated.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Napoleon III sought French prestige and influence across Europe, the Mediterranean and beyond in the manner of the first Empire, and the Napoleonic idea made restoring such standing central.

delink-world-market.rationale: The Second Empire pursued free-trade treaties (Cobden-Chevalier 1860) and foreign investment; inferred that it would not urge poor countries to break from the world market.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Bonapartism claimed to rule above classes and reconcile workers with the order, so it would reject a view of workers as divided by exploitation; anachronistic and inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the strong centralised state and its claim to uphold civil equality under the Napoleonic codes; it would not leave such matters to private owners' unrestricted choice.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1852 constitution gave the executive dominant power with a weak legislature and offered rights only as declared principles of 1789 under the emperor's authority; entrenchment against the executive runs against the model.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; Napoleonic ideology was imperial and indifferent to such claims.

elective-rulers.rationale: Rejects hereditary succession only in form: Napoleon III's rule rested on plebiscites, but it established a hereditary empire.

minority-veto.rationale: Centralised authority and the leader's plebiscitary authority leave no room for minority veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The 1852 constitution made the ruler responsible only to the people through plebiscite and suppressed opposition, which denies a right to resist.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Power was concentrated in the Emperor, with the legislative body made subordinate.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed by the Second Empire; neither a doctrine nor a defining issue.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the era's conventional acceptance of animal use for food and research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Napoleon III's paternalist social policy involved worker housing and mutual aid from above.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The regime demanded active loyalty and national mobilisation, and discouraged withdrawal from public affairs.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not addressed; the regime itself managed the press and used propaganda, but doesn't take a side in this theory.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from its plebiscitary legitimacy and cultivated popular consent alongside force; Marx's analysis cuts the other way.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from its protective, industrialising nationalism, which doesn't adopt a world-system critique.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from its national-glory emphasis and French civic preference, though not stated as policy.

party-own-road.rationale: The statement concerns communist parties; the ideology is not addressed.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Napoleon III pursued state-led growth but also foreign investment and free trade; adherents are split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Napoleonic nationalism sought to revise the 1815 settlement and regain lost French prestige and territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from its imperial outlook, which places no value on pre-colonial peoples' leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Suppressed organised opposition and has no such founding value; it is an authoritarian regime.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; the statement does not fit the Second Empire.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic; the statement concerns the US and was not addressed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from its cult of Napoleonic national glory and tradition.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from its imperial confidence that institutions should be fitted to national character; France's own form is plebiscitary empire.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army was a pillar of the regime, which rested on the military and bureaucracy as guardians of order.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from its paternalism, which treats women's work through the family; the idea is anachronistic.

missingStatements.text: A head of state should be entitled to appeal directly to the people by plebiscite over the heads of parliament.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1851 Appel au peuple and the 1851 and 1852 plebiscites made the direct appeal the regime's legitimating act.

missingStatements.text: A country's legislature should have no power to amend laws proposed by the executive.
missingStatements.rationale: Under the 1852 constitution the Legislative Body could neither amend laws nor censure ministers.

missingStatements.text: Governments should permit freedom of trade between nations by treaty while keeping some tariff protections.
missingStatements.rationale: The 1860 Cobden-Chevalier treaty and related bilateral agreements lowered tariffs while retaining protections.
missingStatements.declined: Existing free-trade and tariffs-protect-industry statements are both answered 0 by this audit (mixed treaty-based policy); a separate statement would be too narrow.

notes: Many answers are low-confidence inferences because Bonapartism is a style of rule more than a programme. Strands differ: Napoleon I's tradition was protectionist and militarist, the Second Empire turned liberal after 1860, and the Marxian sense treats the term as a type of regime rather than a belief system.
